user_authorization: user approved: fixed x86_64 build; KVM, KVM+nopv, TCG, TCG -cpu max boots with QMP CPU hotplug

kernel.config: x86_64_defconfig; record CONFIG_SMP, HOTPLUG_CPU, ACPI_HOTPLUG_CPU, HYPERVISOR_GUEST, PARAVIRT, KVM_GUEST, BLK_DEV_INITRD, DEVTMPFS; enable KVM_GUEST/ACPI_HOTPLUG_CPU/DEVTMPFS only if absent and record the change; LOCALVERSION=-lba-acpi-env

pid1: static C; mounts proc/sysfs/devtmpfs; prints possible/present/online and cpu directories; prints LBA_READY; waits up to 45 s for a new cpuN directory; writes 1 to its online file and reports errno; prints final sets; powers off
hotplug: after LBA_READY: qmp_capabilities, query-hotpluggable-cpus, device_add of the first slot without qom-path using its type and props; record every QMP reply

hypotheses_not_observations.kvm: Hypervisor detected: KVM; possible 0-3; hot-added CPU appears and onlines
hypotheses_not_observations.kvm_nopv: no hypervisor line; possible 0; hot-added CPU does not become usable
hypotheses_not_observations.tcg: no hypervisor line; possible 0; hot-added CPU does not become usable

relations.P1_policy_reach: for a QEMU guest whose legacy MADT carries Enabled=0 hotplug slots, possible at boot covers present plus those slots (commit intent: QEMU use case allowed for guests)
relations.P3_hotplug_consumption: a hot-added CPU becomes online only if it was possible at boot (diagnostic of consequence, not of policy)

stop_rule: failed build or boot is recorded and not silently retried; a corrected rerun is a separate attempt directory
not_claimed: that TCG is in upstream scope; any TCG/nopv loss is a policy-reach observation, not a confirmed defect
